description: An open-source, self-hostable PaaS alternative to Vercel, Heroku & Netlify that lets you easily deploy static sites, databases, full-stack applications and 360+ one-click services on your own servers.

summary.one_liner: Coolify is a self-hostable, open-source platform for deploying applications, databases, and one-click services on your own servers, positioned as an alternative to Heroku, Netlify, and Vercel.
summary.what_it_does: Coolify manages servers, applications, and databases on hardware you control, needing only an SSH connection to each server (VPS, bare metal, Raspberry Pi, or similar). It can build applications from GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, or Gitea using Nixpacks, Railpack, Dockerfile, Docker Compose, or a prebuilt Docker image. It deploys managed databases and more than 360 one-click services with persistent storage and generated credentials. Automation features include deploy-on-push, pull-request previews, deployment webhooks, and rollback to retained images. It also handles custom domains, automatic HTTPS certificates, reverse proxies, health checks, backups, scheduled tasks, environment variables, secrets, notifications, logs, container terminals, and resource monitoring. Access is through a dashboard, API, CLI, MCP, and team-based access controls. The README states that configurations stay on the user's servers and running resources keep working if Coolify is stopped.
use_cases: deploy apps from GitHub or GitLab to my own VPS
run databases and one-click services on my own servers
automatic HTTPS and custom domains for self-hosted apps
manage multiple servers from one dashboard
schedule backups of databases and storage
notable: Deploys to any SSH-accessible server, including Raspberry Pi and bare metal
Over 360 one-click services with persistent storage and generated credentials
Supports Nixpacks, Railpack, Dockerfile, Docker Compose, and prebuilt images
Pull-request previews and rollback to retained application images
Offers a hosted Coolify Cloud option alongside the free self-hosted version
caveats: Self-hosted setup needs a separate server for Coolify and other servers for deployed resources (recommended, not required)
Coolify Cloud is a paid service; pricing is referenced on coolify.io
Install command in README is truncated; the installation guide holds requirements and supported-server details
keywords: deploy apps on my own server
